analysis.title: FX Daily: Time for a break below 1.10 in EUR/USD?
key_insights: EUR/USD is set to test the 1.100 support. ING expects the pair to hold the line this week given a light US data calendar, but sees meaningful risk of a break lower because the USD rally is macro-driven.
Two-year USD swap rates have risen 35bp since Fed's Waller mentioned a 50bp hike and core CPI overshot on 10 November. Other Fed speakers have not countered the hawkish repricing.

ING sees the Fed funds futures curve favouring back-to-back 25bp hikes in December and January, which is more realistic and harder for moderate FOMC members to push back against than an imminent 50bp move. A jump to pricing 50bp in December would make ING more bearish on the dollar.

This week's Fed speakers are not seen as a significant downside risk for the dollar. Chair Warsh speaks today but has been wary of offering guidance outside meetings. October FOMC minutes are due Wednesday.

The larger risk of a USD correction comes from US equities. Nvidia reports earnings tomorrow and Anthropic is expected to debut on the stock market Thursday. Tech has held up well despite Nvidia's idiosyncratic selloff.

Given the size of the front-end rates move and the high bar for further hawkish surprises, ING favours dollar stabilisation over another leg higher, but expects markets to fade dollar corrections for now.

The EUR/USD 2-year swap differential has widened nearly 35bp to its widest since September 2025. Adjusted for 2yr inflation swaps, the real front-end differential is at its widest since December 2022. The euro carries some premium for eurozone fiscal risk.
ING's macro team thinks markets overestimate US inflation risk and will face a large dovish repricing, but not in the near term. ING expects EUR/USD to stabilise in the 1.10-1.11 range.
USD/CAD is close to the October highs (1.430 intraday). A break of 1.430 would technically open the way to 1.450. CAD has outperformed all other G10 currencies over the past week.

Canadian October CPI is due today. ING expects headline at +0.3% m/m, with the yearly rate rising from 3.1% to 3.2%, and median and trim CPI up 0.1ppt, anchored around 2.0%. ING expects a BoC hike more likely in January than December (15bp priced for December).
CEE: ING remains bearish on CEE FX since the end of summer. The US dollar is testing new highs and global energy prices have rebounded, while regional central banks stay dovish.

The National Bank of Hungary decides tomorrow. ING expects no change at 5.50% and a delay in rate cuts. EUR/CZK around 24.400 looks fair after absorbing the CNB's dovishness. EUR/PLN and EUR/HUF likely have more upside.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on 17 November 2026 (tomorrow relative to the 16 November note). It is described as one of two major tests for the AI trade this week.

tension_points.bull_case: ING expects EUR/USD to hold 1.100 in a light US data week and stabilise in the 1.10-1.11 range. Its macro team thinks markets overestimate US inflation risk and will face a large dovish repricing.
tension_points.bear_case: The USD rally is macro-driven, with the 2-year swap differential at its widest since September 2025 and the real front-end differential at its widest since December 2022. A break below 1.100 would be a small stretch relative to short-term fundamentals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below 1.100 in EUR/USD, or markets pricing a 50bp Fed move in December, which would make ING more bearish on the dollar.
